description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color and incredibly comforting flavor. This classic recipe features simple ingredients transformed into a smooth, hearty soup, perfect for a warming meal. Often served with a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of spicy melted butter, it embodies the warmth and hospitality of Turkish cuisine.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Vegetables
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and saute until softened, about 5 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Add the diced carrot and potato to the pot and continue to saute for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they start to soften. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, allowing it to deepen in color and flavor.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Liquid
instructions.text: Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup to Smoothness
instructions.text: Once the lentils and vegetables are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Adjust seasoning if necessary.

instructions.title: Prepare the Butter Topping
instructions.text: While the soup is simmering or after blending, prepare the butter topping. In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and pul biber (Turkish chili flakes). Cook for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Be careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual serving bowls. Drizzle each bowl with a spoonful of the aromatic butter and spice topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side, allowing each person to squeeze lemon juice into their soup to taste.

tips: Always use good quality dried mint and pul biber (Turkish chili flakes) for the authentic flavor in the butter topping. These are crucial for the traditional taste.
A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before serving brightens the flavors and is absolutely essential for a true Mercimek Corbasi experience. Do not skip it!
This soup tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop.
article:
A cornerstone of Turkish culinary tradition, few dishes evoke the warmth and comfort quite like a steaming bowl of Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, wholesome soup is more than just a meal; it's an embrace, a symbol of hospitality, and a staple found on nearly every Turkish table, from bustling city restaurants to cozy family homes. Its rich, earthy flavor, coupled with its creamy texture and nutritional benefits, makes it a beloved choice for breakfast, lunch, or dinner. If you're looking to explore the heartwarming world of Turkish soups and stews, Mercimek Corbasi is the perfect place to start – a simple yet profoundly satisfying dish that captures the essence of Anatolian cooking.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is a classic Turkish soup renowned for its beautiful reddish-orange hue, smooth consistency, and deeply savory taste. Made primarily from red lentils, it's often enriched with a medley of aromatic vegetables like onions, carrots, and sometimes potatoes, all simmered together in a flavorful broth. What truly sets this soup apart is its signature finishing touch: a vibrant drizzle of melted butter infused with dried mint and often a hint of red pepper flakes (pul biber). This simple addition elevates the soup from delicious to extraordinary, adding a layer of fresh, herbaceous warmth and a subtle kick.

Culturally, Mercimek Corbasi holds a special place. It’s a common sight on restaurant menus as a starter, but it's equally enjoyed as a light meal in itself. Many Turks even enjoy it for breakfast, appreciating its comforting and fortifying qualities. Its humble ingredients belie a sophisticated flavor profile that is both nourishing and incredibly satisfying. Beyond its delicious taste, this soup is packed with protein, fiber, and essential nutrients, making it a healthy and fulfilling option for any time of day. Its ability to soothe and satisfy has cemented its status as one of Turkey's most cherished culinary treasures.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting an authentic Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup requires a selection of readily available ingredients, proving that extraordinary flavor often comes from simple components.

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Ensure they are thoroughly rinsed before cooking.
*   **Aromatics:** One large onion, finely chopped, and 2-3 cloves of garlic, minced, form the flavor base.
*   **Vegetables:** One medium carrot, peeled and diced, and one small potato, peeled and diced (optional, but adds body and creaminess).
*   **Liquid:** 6-8 cups of water or vegetable/chicken broth. Using broth will deepen the flavor.
*   **Tomato Paste:** 1-2 tablespoons. A good quality Turkish tomato paste (salça) is ideal for authentic flavor.
*   **Spices:** 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1 teaspoon sweet paprika, and a pinch of black pepper. For heat, add 1/2 teaspoon of pul biber (Aleppo pepper) or red pepper flakes.
*   **Fat:** 2 tablespoons olive oil for sautéing, and 2-3 tablespoons unsalted butter for the final mint infusion.
*   **Garnish:** Fresh lemon wedges, 1-2 teaspoons dried mint for the butter infusion, and extra pul biber for serving.
*   **Salt:** To taste.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, even for beginner cooks. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl every time:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in the diced carrot and potato (if using), and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Stir in the ground cumin, paprika, and black pepper (and pul biber if using), and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the vegetables and spices. Pour in the water or broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend the Soup:** Once the lentils and vegetables are cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. If you don't have an immersion blender, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth. Return the blended soup to the pot.
6.  **Season and Adjust Consistency:** Return the pot to low heat. Season generously with salt to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Let it gently simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
7.  **Prepare the Mint Infusion (Nane Yağı):** While the soup is simmering, melt the unsalted butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, add the dried mint (and optional pul biber). Cook for about 30 seconds until the mint becomes fragrant, being careful not to burn it.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the warm mint-infused butter over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, comforting bowl of Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is easy with a few expert tricks up your sleeve:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial! Rinsing removes starches that can make your soup cloudy and sometimes bitter. Keep rinsing until the water runs clear.
*   **Sauté Aromatics Well:** Don't rush the initial sautéing of onions and garlic. Allowing them to soften and lightly caramelize builds a crucial depth of flavor for your soup.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** Cooking the tomato paste and spices for a minute or two before adding the liquid "blooms" them, intensifying their aroma and taste.
*   **Blend Until Smooth:** For that signature creamy texture, blend the soup until it’s absolutely smooth. No chunky bits should remain. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **Don't Skip the Lemon:** The fresh squeeze of lemon juice added just before eating is non-negotiable. It brightens the soup, cuts through the richness, and truly awakens all the flavors.
*   **The Mint Butter is Key:** The *nane yağı* (mint-infused butter) isn't just a garnish; it's an essential flavor component that provides a fragrant, savory finish. Don't burn the mint!
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils tend to thicken as they cool. Feel free to add a splash of hot water or broth when reheating or if you prefer a thinner soup.

## Serving Suggestions

Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways. Traditionally, it’s served piping hot, garnished with a generous drizzle of the fragrant mint-infused butter and a fresh lemon wedge. Squeezing the lemon juice directly into your bowl just before eating is a must, as it adds a vital tangy counterpoint to the earthy lentils.

Alongside your bowl of Mercimek Corbasi, consider serving:

*   **Fresh Bread:** A crusty loaf of Turkish bread (pide), a sesame-crusted simit, or even a simple slice of sourdough is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop.
*   **Pickles:** Turkish cuisine often pairs soups with a small plate of assorted pickles (turşu), which offer a refreshing crunch and tangy contrast.
*   **Olives:** A few salty Turkish olives can complement the soup beautifully.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For those who love heat, offer extra pul biber (Aleppo pepper flakes) at the table for guests to sprinkle on top.

Whether enjoyed as a comforting starter to a larger meal or as a light yet satisfying meal in itself, this Turkish classic is always a crowd-pleaser.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Make it Vegan:** Easily done! Simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth, and substitute olive oil or a plant-based butter alternative for the butter in the mint infusion.
*   **Add More Vegetables:** Feel free to incorporate other finely diced vegetables like celery, bell peppers, or even a small amount of zucchini during the sautéing stage for added nutrients and flavor complexity.
*   **Spice It Up:** If you prefer a bolder flavor profile, increase the amount of pul biber or add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the other spices. A touch of smoked paprika can also add an interesting depth.
*   **Herbaceous Twists:** While dried mint is traditional, you can also experiment with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or dill as a garnish for a different fresh note.
*   **Thickening Agent:** For an even heartier soup, some recipes include a tablespoon of rice or bulgur cooked along with the lentils, which also helps thicken the soup.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are standard, you could try using split yellow lentils for a similar texture and mild flavor, though the color will be different. Green or brown lentils will yield a very different texture and require longer cooking times, so they are not recommended for this specific soup.

No matter how you choose to personalize it, the core comforting essence of Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup remains.

In conclusion, Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup is more than just a recipe; it's an invitation to experience the heart of Turkish home cooking. Its simplicity, combined with its profound depth of flavor and nourishing qualities, makes it a truly special dish. Whether you're seeking comfort on a chilly evening, a healthy and quick meal, or simply a taste of authentic Turkish cuisine, this vibrant red lentil soup is sure to become a beloved addition to your culinary repertoire. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the warmth and flavor of this timeless classic.
